analysis: The supplied units are base-side excerpts (lines 6862-9139) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, a test-vector fixture holding request bodies, template inputs, prompt-contract plans and token_ids for the Qwen3.8-27B prompt contract. The patch excerpt shows the PR adds an `additional_context: {enable_thinking: false}` member to template inputs, shortens token sequences (prompt_token_count 803→767) and recomputes chain hashes. Changed ranges at base lines such as 43813 and 52418 lie outside the supplied excerpts, so I could not see those hunks. The visible base text, including the `tools` vector that already carries additional_context, is data only and has no executable behavior, authentication, key handling or network surface. Threat-model relevance: it touches prompt-contract and prefix-cache chain hashes (T-041, TB-007), because block-boundary hashes bind cache identity to prompt tokens. A fixture change that is consistently regenerated on the Go and Swift sides is not a regression by itself. Open integration questions: (1) whether the PR's production code (Swift prompt renderer and Go coordinator planner) changes the template rendering for enable_thinking consistently, so that the prompt_contract_id and cache scope keys cannot collide or diverge across tool/no-tool requests; (2) the prompt_contract_id (8171fec3...) appears unchanged in the visible portions even though rendering output changed, so integration should check whether the ID is meant to version the template and whether stale cached prefixes could be reused across the changed rendering. I treat both as unverified contracts, not findings. No secrets or credentials appear in the fixture.
